sentence: ¿Por qué no abandonamos a Tom?
why: the English “Why don't we” shows a suggestion about what to do now, so it is the present.

sentence: Mi abuela abogaba por comer en familia todos los domingos.
why: its subject is “mi abuela” (my grandmother), and “todos los domingos” (every Sunday) marks a past habit, so it is the imperfect.

sentence: Abre la llave del agua, por favor.
why: it is a request with “por favor” (please) to turn on the tap, a command to tú.

sentence: La puerta no abre.
why: the subject is “La puerta” (the door), and “no abre” (won't open) describes it now.

sentence: El negro absorbe la luz.
why: its subject is “El negro” (black), and it states a general fact, so it is the present indicative.

sentence: Él aburre a todo el mundo.
why: its subject is “Él” (he), and the present describes his general effect on people.

sentence: No abuses de la sal en la comida.
why: “No abuses” (don't overdo) tells “tú” directly not to do something, and negative commands use this form.

sentence: Siempre acabamos comiendo en el mismo lugar.
why: the English “We always end up” and “Siempre” (always) describe a regular habit in the present.

sentence: Sí, pero ella se acaba de ir.
why: the subject is “ella” (she), and “se acaba de ir” (has just left) uses the present of “acabar de” for something that has just happened.

sentence: Un ladrón acechaba en el oscuro pasillo.
why: its subject is “Un ladrón” (a thief), and it describes an ongoing situation in the past, so it is the imperfect.

sentence: ¿Qué acecha en las sombras?
why: its subject is “Qué” (what), and the English “is lurking” asks about now, so it is the present indicative.

sentence: Mi corazón se acelera cada vez que la veo.
why: its subject is “Mi corazón” (my heart), and “cada vez que” (each time) marks a present habit.

sentence: Acepta las cosas como son.
why: the English “Take things as they are” is advice given as a command to tú.

sentence: El Año Nuevo se acercaba.
why: the subject is “El Año Nuevo” (the New Year), and the imperfect describes it drawing near over time in the past.

sentence: Gana el que acierte el número.
why: its subject is “el que” (whoever), a person not yet known, so the relative clause takes the subjunctive.

sentence: Esta música se acomoda a mi humor en este momento.
why: its subject is “Esta música” (this music), and “en este momento” (at the moment) points to now, so it is the present indicative.

sentence: Nos mudamos a esta casa el mes pasado, pero todavía no nos acomodamos.
why: “todavía no” (not yet) with the English “haven't settled” marks a change yet to happen, which Latin American Spanish puts in the preterite, like “Nos mudamos” (we moved).

sentence: A Tom lo acompañaba Mary.
why: its subject is “Mary”, placed after the verb, and the imperfect describes her accompanying Tom at the time.

sentence: Le dijeron que me acompañara.
why: a reported request after “Le dijeron que” takes the subjunctive, and its subject is the person told, “Le” (her); “me” is the one accompanied.

sentence: No tienen a nadie que los aconseje.
why: in “a nadie que…” (no one who…), a person who doesn't exist calls for the subjunctive, and its subject is “nadie”, third person singular.

sentence: Él todavía se acuerda de ti.
why: the subject is “Él” (he), and “todavía se acuerda de ti” (still remembers you) describes him now.

sentence: Uno se acostumbra a todo.
why: its subject is “Uno” (one), which takes a third-person singular verb, in a general present statement.

sentence: Actúa en vez de hablar.
why: the English “Act. Don't talk.” is a command, telling tú to act “en vez de hablar” (instead of talking).

sentence: Mi prima actúa en una telenovela muy famosa.
why: its subject is “Mi prima” (my cousin), and the sentence states what she does, so it is the present indicative.

sentence: No actúes como si no supieras lo que está pasando.
why: it directly tells tú not to act that way, with “No actúes” (don't act), and negative commands use this form.

sentence: Acude primero a aquellos de los que estás seguro de que te ayudarán.
why: the sentence opens with the verb and tells the listener where to go first, and “estás seguro” (you are sure) shows it is a command to tú.

sentence: El trabajo se acumula.
why: its subject is “El trabajo” (the work), and it says what is happening now, so it is the present indicative.

sentence: ¿Por qué acusa a mi hijo?
why: it asks a question (“¿Por qué…?”, why) about what the person addressed is doing, and the English “do you accuse” shows the subject is usted.

sentence: Pero, a medida que se adentraba en la lectura de la obra completa de Bonet, Tosar vio la necesidad de ampliar la dimensión del espectáculo.
why: its subject is “Tosar”, who “vio” (saw) the need; “a medida que” (as) gives the ongoing background of his reading, so it is the imperfect.

sentence: Adivina lo que quiere Tom.
why: the sentence opens with the verb and tells the listener to guess (“Guess what Tom wants”), so it is a command to tú.

sentence: Administraba los intereses de su amigo.
why: no subject is named, and the English “He administered” makes it third person; the imperfect describes his ongoing role in the past.

sentence: Nadie lo admira más que yo.
why: its subject is “Nadie” (no one), which takes a third-person singular verb, and the present states a current feeling.

sentence: No admitas nunca que le quieres.
why: it directly tells tú never to admit it, with “No admitas nunca” (never admit), and negative commands use this form.

sentence: De niño adoraba a su padre.
why: “su padre” (his father) and the English “When he was a child he loved” show the subject is he, and the imperfect describes a past state.

sentence: Tú eres el que adora al dinero.
why: its subject is “el que” (the one who), which takes a third-person singular verb, and the present describes what that person adores now.

sentence: La ciudad brilla siempre, lámparas reemplazan al sol. Su imagen adorna el horizonte profundo.
why: its subject is “Su imagen” (its image), and the passage describes the city in the present, “brilla” (glows), so it is the present indicative.

sentence: Cada vez, la historia de Tom adquiría más detalles.
why: its subject is “la historia de Tom” (Tom's story), and “Cada vez” (each time) with the imperfect describes a repeated past development.

sentence: No dejes que esos problemas te afecten.
why: letting something happen, “dejes que”, calls for the subjunctive, and its subject is “esos problemas” (those problems).

sentence: Ya no me afecta lo que digas.
why: like “gustar”, its subject is “lo que digas” (what you say), with “me” as the person, so it is third person singular, in the present.

sentence: Él se afeita todos los días.
why: its subject is “Él” (he), and “todos los días” (every day) marks a habit, so it is the present indicative.

sentence: Ella se aferraba a su papá.
why: its subject is “Ella” (she), and the English “was clinging” shows an ongoing action in the past, so it is the imperfect.

sentence: Él afirma que no sabe nada acerca de ella.
why: the subject is “Él” (he), and “afirma que” (claims that) is a statement about now.

sentence: Se espera que su expedición afronte problemas.
why: its subject is “su expedición” (the expedition), and “Se espera que” (it is expected that) looks ahead to something uncertain, which takes the subjunctive.

sentence: ¡Afronta la vida con una sonrisa!
why: it is an exclamatory command, “¡Afronta la vida…!” (face life), addressed to one person as tú.

sentence: Agachen la cabeza que el techo es muy bajo.
why: it is a command to several people, “Agachen la cabeza” (lower your heads), with the reason after “que” (since), so it is the ustedes command.

sentence: Tom se agachaba al lado de Mary.
why: its subject is “Tom”, and it describes what he was doing at a moment in the past, so it is the imperfect.

sentence: A Mary le agrada ella.
why: with agradar the thing liked is the subject, here “ella” (her), while “A Mary le” marks who likes it; the present describes a current feeling.

sentence: Esto se agrega a mis problemas.
why: its subject is “Esto” (this), with “se agrega” (is added) describing a present situation.

sentence: Agrupa las palabras según su significado.
why: it is an instruction, “Agrupa las palabras” (group the words), to one person, as in an exercise, so it is the tú command.

sentence: Este puente aguanta el peso de los camiones.
why: the subject is “Este puente” (this bridge), and the sentence describes what it can bear now.

sentence: Aguarde un momento, por favor.
why: “por favor” (please) with the verb first makes a polite command, and the -e ending of this -ar verb shows it is addressed to usted.

sentence: Me dijeron que aguardara un momento.
why: after the past “Me dijeron que” (told me to), a reported request, the imperfect subjunctive is used, and the one told, “Me”, is its subject.

sentence: ¿Qué te aguarda en Nueva York?
why: its subject is “Qué” (what), and the present asks what awaits the listener in New York now.

sentence: Él ahorra lo que gana.
why: its subject is “Él” (he), and the present describes his habit.

sentence: Ajusta la hora del reloj.
why: the sentence opens with the verb and tells the listener what to do with the clock (“Ajusta la hora”, adjust the time), so it is a command to tú.

sentence: El museo alberga miles de piezas de oro.
why: its subject is “el museo” (the museum), and it states a present fact, so it is the present indicative.

sentence: ¿Hay algún albergue juvenil cerca de aquí?
why: “algún albergue juvenil” (a youth hostel) contains the noun albergue (hostel), not a form of the verb albergar.

sentence: La familia de Tom se alegra de que haya vuelto.
why: the subject is “La familia de Tom” (Tom's family), and “se alegra” (is happy) describes it now.

sentence: Nos alegramos de tenerte con nosotros.
why: the English “We're glad” shows a feeling the speakers have now, so it is the present.

sentence: Aleja a Tom de mi.
why: the English “Get Tom away from me” is a direct command, addressed to tú.

sentence: Ella es la que alimenta a nuestro perro.
why: its subject is “la que” (the one who), referring to “Ella” (she), and the present describes a regular task.

sentence: Nunca dejo que nadie más alimente a mi perro.
why: after “dejo que” (let), the verb takes the subjunctive, and its subject is “nadie más” (anyone else), third person singular.

sentence: ¿Hay alguna cosa que te alivie el dolor?
why: in “alguna cosa que…” (anything that…), a question about whether such a thing exists calls for the subjunctive, and its subject is that thing.

sentence: ¿Por qué él ya no almuerza conmigo?
why: its subject is “él” (he), and “ya no” (no longer) describes his present habit.

sentence: Tom alquila habitaciones para estudiantes.
why: its subject is “Tom”, and the present describes his regular business.

sentence: No se altere usted que no es nada.
why: “No se altere usted” is a direct command telling “usted” not to get upset, and negative commands use this form.

sentence: El artículo alude a un evento ya olvidado.
why: its subject is “El artículo” (the article), and it describes what the article contains, so it is the present indicative.

sentence: Si tienes una pregunta, alza la mano, por favor.
why: after “Si tienes una pregunta” (if you have a question), it tells the listener what to do (“por favor”, please), so it is a command to tú.

sentence: ¡No me alces la mano!
why: “¡No me alces la mano!” is a direct command telling tú not to raise a hand, and negative commands use this form.

sentence: Ella sabe que John la amaba.
why: its subject is “John” in “que John la amaba” (that John loved her), and the imperfect describes his lasting feeling in the past.

sentence: Yo sé que Mary me ama.
why: its subject is “Mary” in “que Mary me ama” (that Mary loves me), a statement about now.

sentence: Mi reloj no anda, necesita pila.
why: the subject is “Mi reloj” (my watch), and “no anda” (isn't working) describes it now.

sentence: Ahora anochece a las cinco.
why: the verb is impersonal, about nightfall (“It gets dark”), so it is third person singular, and “Ahora” (now) makes it the present indicative.

sentence: ¿No estás segura de que vayan a poder localizarnos antes de que anochezca?
why: “antes de que” (before) always takes the subjunctive, and the verb is impersonal, about nightfall, so it is third person singular.

sentence: Anota lo que está diciendo, por favor.
why: the sentence opens with the verb and asks the listener to write something down (“por favor”, please), so it is a command to tú.

sentence: Pedimos que anulen esta ley.
why: the request “Pedimos que” (request that) takes the subjunctive; no subject is named, and the English “that they repeal” makes it third person plural.

sentence: Esa empresa anuncia sus productos en la radio.
why: the subject is “Esa empresa” (that company), and the sentence describes its regular practice now.

sentence: Mi hermana dijo que anunciaría la fecha de su boda pronto.
why: its subject is “mi hermana” (my sister), who “dijo que” (said that) she would announce it; the conditional gives the future seen from the past.

sentence: Apaga la luz al salir de la habitación.
why: the English “Turn off the light” is an instruction, addressed to tú.

sentence: Apaga la vela antes de dormir.
why: the English “Blow out the candle” is an instruction, addressed to tú.

sentence: ¿Querés que apague las luces?
why: the wish in “Querés que” calls for the subjunctive, and the English “want me to turn off” shows its subject is yo.

sentence: Dile a él que aparezca.
why: the embedded request after “Dile a él que” (tell him to) takes the subjunctive, and its subject is “él” (him), the one who should show up.

sentence: Pensé que Tom se aparecería.
why: its subject is “Tom”, and the conditional, after the past “Pensé que” (thought that), describes what was expected to happen later.

sentence: No sé nada de él aparte de su nombre.
why: here “aparte de” (apart from) is the adverb aparte, not a form of the verb apartar.

sentence: Su indefensión apela a su compasión maternal.
why: its subject is “Su indefensión” (his helplessness), and it states a present fact, so it is the present indicative.

sentence: Ese programa apesta, no lo vuelvo a ver.
why: its subject is “Ese programa” (that show), and the present gives the speaker's current opinion.

sentence: Nadie quería jugar con Tango, excepto el pequeño niño, porque Tango apestaba.
why: its subject is “Tango”, and the imperfect describes a past state that explains “Nadie quería” (no one wanted).

sentence: No voy a comer algo que apeste así.
why: in “algo que…” (something that…), a thing not known to exist after “No voy a comer” calls for the subjunctive, and its subject is “algo”.

sentence: ¡El sujeto sentado junto a mí en el tren apesta!
why: its subject is “El sujeto” (the guy), and the present describes the situation now.

sentence: A Sami le apetecía un poco irse a casa.
why: with apetecer the thing wanted is the subject, here “irse a casa” (going home), so the verb is third-person singular, and the imperfect describes Sami's past wish.

sentence: No sé qué hacer, ahora mismo no me apetece hacer nada.
why: with apetecer the thing wanted is the subject, here “hacer nada” (doing anything), so the verb is third-person singular, in the present (“ahora mismo”, right now).

sentence: Lo que dijo no aplica en esta situación.
why: its subject is “Lo que dijo” (what he said), and the present states that it doesn't apply in this situation now.

sentence: Están esperando a que yo aporte ideas.
why: after “esperando a que” (waiting for), the subjunctive is used, and its subject is “yo” (I).

sentence: ¿Por qué no aportamos todos nosotros treinta dólares?
why: “¿Por qué no…?” (why don't) with the present makes a suggestion, and “todos nosotros” (all of us) is the subject.

sentence: Yo no apostaría contra Tom.
why: the subject is “Yo” (I), and the conditional expresses what the speaker would do.

sentence: ¿Por quién quieres que apueste?
why: after “quieres que” (do you want … to) the subjunctive is used, and the English “want me to bet” shows the speaker is the subject.

sentence: Apoya la escalera contra la pared, por favor.
why: it is a request with “por favor” (please) to lean the ladder against the wall, a command to tú.

sentence: ¡No te apoyes en la puerta!
why: it directly tells tú not to lean on the door, with “No te apoyes” (don't lean), and negative commands use this form.

sentence: No apresure el paso; llegaremos a la hora.
why: “No apresure el paso” is a direct command telling usted not to hurry, and negative commands use this form.

sentence: El avión se aproximaba a Londres.
why: its subject is “El avión” (the plane), and the imperfect describes an ongoing past action (“was approaching”).

sentence: Apunta la linterna hacia la puerta.
why: the English “Point the flashlight” is a command, addressed to tú.

sentence: Si nos apuramos, creo que la hacemos.
why: “Si” (if) introducing a real condition takes the present, and the English “if we hurry” shows the subject is we.

sentence: Mi hermana argumenta que el perro necesita más espacio.
why: its subject is “mi hermana” (my sister), and it states what she argues now, so it is the present indicative.

sentence: Smith argumenta que no existen leyes internacionales que puedan aplicarse a este caso.
why: its subject is “Smith”, and it reports his current position, so it is the present indicative.

sentence: ¡No arrastres la mesa! Levántala y luego la mueves.
why: “¡No arrastres la mesa!” is a direct command telling tú not to drag the table, and negative commands use this form.

sentence: Quiero que arresten a Tom.
why: after “Quiero que” (want … to), a wish, the subjunctive is used; no subject is named and the arrest is made by unnamed people, so it is the impersonal third-person plural.

sentence: No arriesgues tu vida por mí.
why: “No arriesgues” is a direct command telling tú not to risk a life, and negative commands use this form.

sentence: Todo esto arroja nuevas preguntas.
why: its subject is “Todo esto” (all this), and the present describes the current result.

sentence: El dinero arruina a muchos.
why: the subject is “El dinero” (money), and the saying states a timeless truth in the present.

sentence: Siempre me asalta el hambre a medianoche.
why: its subject is “el hambre” (hunger), and “siempre” (always) marks a present habit, so it is the present indicative.

sentence: Asegura bien la puerta antes de salir.
why: the sentence opens with the verb, names no subject and tells the listener to lock the door (“Lock the door”), so it is a command to tú.

sentence: Se suponía que ella asistiera a la fiesta con él.
why: after the past “Se suponía que” (was supposed to), the imperfect subjunctive is used, and its subject is “ella” (she).

sentence: Él asiste a la misma escuela que yo.
why: its subject is “Él” (he), and the present describes the school he attends now.

sentence: A menudo asociamos el negro con la muerte.
why: “A menudo” (often) marks a present habit, and the English “We often associate” shows the subject is we.

sentence: Solo se asocia con gente prestigiosa.
why: no subject is named, and the English “He associates” shows it is he; “Solo” (only) with the present describes his habit.

sentence: Todos nos asomamos a la ventana para ver qué pasaba.
why: with “Todos nos” (we all) as subject, “qué pasaba” (what was happening) and the English “looked” mark one completed action in the past, so it is the preterite.

sentence: Nosotros aspiramos a la felicidad.
why: its subject is “Nosotros” (we), and the English “We seek” states a general, ongoing aim, so it is the present indicative.

sentence: En el segundo tiempo atacamos mucho más.
why: the English “we attacked” places it in a match already played, “en el segundo tiempo” (in the second half), a completed action, so it is the preterite.

sentence: Es mejor que el equipo ataque por la derecha.
why: “es mejor que” (it's better that) calls for the subjunctive, and its subject is “el equipo” (the team), third person singular.

sentence: Lo atamos para que así no pudiera escapar.
why: the following “pudiera” (could) is past, and the English “We tied him up” shows a completed past action, so it is the preterite.

sentence: Al perro de Iván le aterrorizaba algo.
why: its subject is “algo” (something), which frightened “Al perro de Iván” (Ivan's dog), and it describes an ongoing state in the past, so it is the imperfect.

sentence: La vida en el campo me atrae mucho.
why: its subject is “La vida en el campo” (rural life), and the present states a current feeling.

sentence: Que no te atrapen.
why: a wish introduced by “Que” takes the subjunctive, and its unnamed subject is “they”, the people who might catch the listener, as the English passive shows.

sentence: Si quiere usted hacer el trabajo bien, no se atropelle.
why: it tells “usted” directly not to rush, “no se atropelle” (don't rush), and negative commands use this form.

sentence: ¿Me autorizaría a grabar esta conversación?
why: it is a polite request to the listener, and the English “Would you authorize me” shows the subject is usted.

sentence: Avanza un poco, que hay espacio atrás.
why: the English “Move forward a bit” is a command, and “que hay espacio atrás” (there's room behind) gives the reason; it addresses tú.

sentence: El tiempo pasaba rápido y el trabajo no avanzaba nada.
why: the subject is “el trabajo” (the work), and the imperfect, like “pasaba” (was passing), describes an ongoing situation in the past.

sentence: No avanzamos nada en nuestro trabajo.
why: the English “We're not making any progress” shows a situation going on now, so it is the present.

sentence: Nunca nos avergonzamos de ti.
why: the English “We were never ashamed of you” puts the sentence in the past, so “Nunca nos avergonzamos” is the preterite with subject we.

sentence: Averigua a dónde fue Tom.
why: the English “Find out where Tom went” is a command, addressed to tú.

sentence: Ella quiere que la ayude.
why: the wish in “quiere que” calls for the subjunctive, and the English “wants me to help her” shows its subject is yo.

sentence: ¿Qué tal si le añadimos un poco más de sal?
why: the suggestion “Qué tal si” (how about) proposes doing something now, so it is the present.

sentence: Barre el suelo, por favor.
why: it is a request to one person, “Barre el suelo, por favor” (sweep the floor, please), so it is the tú command.

sentence: La obra se basa en hechos reales.
why: its subject is “La obra” (the play), and the present describes what it is based on.

sentence: No es difícil. Basta con saber cómo hacerlo.
why: impersonal “Basta con” (it is enough to) has no personal subject and takes the third person singular, in the present like “No es difícil”.

sentence: Nunca digas la verdad cuando una buena mentira baste.
why: the open “cuando” (whenever) about future occasions calls for the subjunctive, and its subject is “una buena mentira” (a good lie).

sentence: Bate las claras de huevo hasta que estén duras.
why: the sentence opens with the verb and tells the cook what to do with the egg whites (“Whip”), so it is a command to tú.

sentence: Me pregunto quién bautizaría a este barco.
why: its subject is “quién” (who), and after “Me pregunto” (wonder) the conditional expresses a guess about who it was.

sentence: Nos bañamos todos los días.
why: “todos los días” (every day) marks a present habit, and “Nos” goes with the subject we.

sentence: No sabía que él bebiera tanto.
why: its subject is “él” (he), and the negated “No sabía que” (didn't know that) puts the clause in the subjunctive.

sentence: Mi abuela siempre nos bendice antes del viaje.
why: its subject is “Mi abuela” (my grandmother), and “siempre” (always) marks a present habit.

sentence: Alguien más se beneficia de la situación.
why: its subject is “Alguien más” (someone else), and the present describes the current situation.

sentence: Escoge aquellos amigos que te beneficien.
why: in “aquellos amigos que…” (such friends as…), friends not yet identified call for the subjunctive, and its plural subject is those friends.

sentence: Él dejó que lo besara.
why: letting someone act, “dejó que”, calls for the subjunctive, and the English “He let her kiss him” shows its subject is “her”.

sentence: Mi madre bordaba lágrimas desiertas en los primeros arcoíris.
why: its subject is “madre” (mother), and the English “was embroidering” shows an ongoing action in the past, so it is the imperfect.

sentence: Tom lanzó el ancla por la borda.
why: “por la borda” (overboard) contains the noun borda (gunwale), not a form of the verb bordar (to embroider).

sentence: ¡Que se borre su nombre!
why: “¡Que…!” at the start expresses a wish and takes the subjunctive, and its subject is “su nombre” (his name).

sentence: El Sol brilla para todos.
why: its subject is “El Sol” (the sun), and the present states a general truth.

sentence: Esta campaña no puede evitar nuevos brotes del virus Zika.
why: “nuevos brotes del virus” (new outbreaks of the virus) contains the noun brote (outbreak), not a form of the verb brotar.

sentence: No eres el que buscamos.
why: the English “we're after” and “No eres” in the main clause show the search is going on now.

sentence: ¿Qué es lo que buscaba Tom?
why: its subject is “Tom”, and the imperfect describes what he was looking for at the time.

sentence: Seguro que cabe, pero hay que pensar cómo meterlo.
why: the subject is the object being discussed (“It sure fits”), and the present states a current fact.

sentence: Te lo puedes meter por donde te quepa.
why: its subject is the thing meant by “lo” (it), and “por donde” (wherever) about an open place takes the subjunctive.

sentence: El traje le cae bien.
why: the subject is “El traje” (the suit), and “le cae bien” (suits him) describes it now.

sentence: Calcule usted a cuánto sale.
why: “Calcule usted” opens the sentence as an instruction to “usted”, so it is the command to usted.

sentence: Su capacidad lo califica para el trabajo.
why: its subject is “Su capacidad” (his skill), and the present states a current fact.

sentence: Solo quería que Tom se callara.
why: the wish in “quería que” (wanted) calls for the subjunctive, and its subject is “Tom”, the one who should shut up.

sentence: ¿Por qué no cancelamos la fiesta?
why: “¿Por qué no…?” (why don't) with the present makes a suggestion, and the English “Why don't we cancel” shows the subject is we.

sentence: Caminar tanto me cansa mucho.
why: its subject is the infinitive phrase “Caminar tanto” (walking so much), which takes a third-person singular verb, in the present.

sentence: La novela latinoamericana se caracteriza por sus contrastes.

sentence: A Tom le duele el oído.
why: like “gustar”, its subject is the body part that hurts, “el oído” (the ear), with “A Tom” as the person, in the present.

sentence: ¿Realmente quieres que done todas tus cosas?
why: “quieres que” (want … to) takes the subjunctive; no subject is named, and the English “want me to give away” makes it yo.

sentence: Dora es una exploradora.
why: the word “Dora” here is a person's name, not a form of the verb dorar (to gild).

sentence: Miguel se lo dio a Dora.
why: the word “Dora” here is a person's name, not a form of the verb dorar (to gild).

sentence: Una cara bonita es la mitad de la dote.
why: “la dote” here is the noun “dowry”, not a form of the verb dotar (to endow).

sentence: El viaje duraba una semana.
why: its subject is “El viaje” (the trip), and the imperfect describes how long it lasted in the past.

sentence: Este artículo necesita que lo editen.
why: “necesita que” (needs … to) takes the subjunctive, and with no subject named the third person plural means people in general.

sentence: ¿Cómo educa a sus hijos?
why: no subject is named, and the English “How does he bring up” shows it is he; the present asks about his habit.

sentence: El mago efectúa varios trucos con cartas.
why: its subject is “El mago” (the magician), and the present describes what he does.

sentence: La sociedad ejerce una gran influencia sobre los individuos.
why: its subject is “La sociedad” (society), and the present states a general truth.

sentence: Aprender a tocar un instrumento ejercita la mente.
why: its subject is the phrase “Aprender a tocar un instrumento” (learning to play an instrument), and it states a general truth, so it is the present indicative.

sentence: Se torció el tobillo mientras se ejercitaba.
why: no subject is named, and the English “while she was doing exercise” makes it third person; “mientras” (while) gives the ongoing background, so it is the imperfect.

sentence: Elige el que quieras.
why: the English “Choose whichever you want” is a command, and “quieras” shows it is addressed to tú.

sentence: El viento eleva las hojas.
why: its subject is “El viento” (the wind), and the present describes what it does.

sentence: Ella siempre llora cuando él se emborracha.
why: its subject is “él” (he), and with “siempre” (always), “cuando” (when) describes a repeated situation rather than a future one, so it is the present indicative.

sentence: Cuando la masa deforme emergía de las sombras, yo sabía que estaba en problemas.
why: its subject is “la masa deforme” (the shapeless mass), and it describes an ongoing action in the past, so it is the imperfect.

sentence: La pantalla solo emite luz verde.
why: its subject is “La pantalla” (the screen), and the present describes what it gives off now.

sentence: El dinero no me emociona. Me relaja.
why: its subject is “El dinero” (money), and it states a general fact about the speaker, so it is the present indicative.

sentence: Tom no quiere que Mary se emocione demasiado.
why: its subject is “Mary”, and “no quiere que” (doesn't want … to) expresses a wish, which takes the subjunctive.

sentence: Está dañado el empaque de este producto.
why: “el empaque” here is the noun “packaging”, not a form of the verb empacar (to pack).

sentence: La vida empieza cuando decides lo que esperas de ella.
why: the subject is “La vida” (life), and the sentence states a general truth in the present.

sentence: Emplea menos tiempo en el inglés que yo.
why: the English “He spends less time on English than me” shows a statement whose subject is he, in the present.

sentence: Muestra siempre mucha decisión en todo lo que emprende.
why: no subject is named, and the English “everything he undertakes” makes it third person; “todo lo que” (everything that) means what he actually takes on, so it is the indicative.

sentence: Sea lo que sea que emprendamos, la diligencia es importante.
why: after “Sea lo que sea que” (whatever), which introduces something not yet known, the subjunctive is used, and the English “we may undertake” gives the subject.

sentence: Me temo que esta llave no encaja.
why: its subject is “esta llave” (this key), and the present describes the current problem.

sentence: Deja que se encarguen ellos.
why: letting someone act, “Deja que”, calls for the subjunctive, and its subject is “ellos” (they).

sentence: Enciende el fuego con estos fósforos.
why: the English “Light the fire” is a command, addressed to tú.

sentence: Enciende las luces, si no, no puedo trabajar.
why: the English “Turn the lights on” is a command, addressed to tú.

sentence: Este libro encierra muchas lecciones valiosas.
why: the subject is “Este libro” (this book), and the sentence states what it contains now.

sentence: ¿El Sr. Al-Obaid se encuentra aquí?
why: the subject is “El Sr. Al-Obaid” (Mr. Al-Obaid), and the question asks whether he is “aquí” (here) now.

sentence: Su sonrisa encubre un poco de tristeza.
why: its subject is “su sonrisa” (her smile), and it describes the present, so it is the present indicative.

sentence: No quiero que Tom se enferme.
why: after “No quiero que” (don't want … to), a wish, the subjunctive is used, and its subject is “Tom”.

sentence: Enfoca el microscopio.
why: the sentence opens with the verb and tells the listener to focus the microscope (“Enfoca el microscopio”), so it is a command to tú.

sentence: Comé la cena antes de que se enfríe.
why: its subject is “la cena” (dinner), and “antes de que” (before) always takes the subjunctive.

sentence: Engancha tu vagón a una estrella.
why: it is a command, “Engancha tu vagón a una estrella” (hitch your wagon to a star), to one person, so it is the tú command.

sentence: Ese tipo me enloquece.
why: its subject is “Ese tipo” (that guy), and the present describes his current effect.

sentence: Me enoja que siempre llegues tarde.
why: its subject is the clause “que siempre llegues tarde” (that you always arrive late), with “Me” as the person, so it is third person singular.

sentence: No quiero que ella se enoje.
why: the wish in “No quiero que” calls for the subjunctive, and its subject is “ella” (she).

sentence: No se lo enseñes a Tom.
why: it directly tells tú not to show it to Tom, with “No se lo enseñes” (don't show it), and negative commands use this form.

sentence: Ella no lo entiende.
why: the subject is “Ella” (she), and “no lo entiende” (doesn't understand it) is a statement about now.

sentence: Sólo dile a Tom de lo que nos enteramos.
why: the English “what we found out” shows a completed discovery in the past, so it is the preterite.

sentence: Ese sofá no entra por la puerta.
why: the subject is “Ese sofá” (that sofa), and “no entra por la puerta” (doesn't fit through the door) describes it now.

sentence: Por favor, entren de uno en uno.
why: it directly asks the group to come in, with “Por favor” (please) and “de uno en uno” (one by one), a command to ustedes.

sentence: Ella me pidió que te entregara esto.
why: the request in “me pidió que” (asked me to) calls for the subjunctive, and the person asked, “me”, is its subject, so it is yo.

sentence: Ayer entrevistamos a algunos turistas de todo el mundo.
why: “Ayer” (yesterday) marks a completed past event, so it is the preterite with subject we.

sentence: A medida que uno envejece cambian los intereses.
why: its subject is “uno” (one), and “A medida que” (as) describes a general process rather than a future event, so it is the present indicative.

sentence: Le pedí que no envenenara el ambiente con sus quejas.
why: “le pedí que no …” (I asked him not to …) is a reported request, which takes the subjunctive, past after “pedí”; the one asked, “le” (him), is its subject.

sentence: Le pedí que nos enviara el libro.
why: the request in “Le pedí que” (asked her to) takes the subjunctive, and its subject is “le” (her), the person asked to send the book.

sentence: Ella envidiaba el éxito de su primo.
why: its subject is “Ella” (she), and it describes an ongoing feeling in the past, so it is the imperfect.

sentence: A él siempre lo envolvía un aire de peligro.
why: its subject is “un aire de peligro” (an air of danger), placed after the verb, and “siempre” (always) with the imperfect describes a lasting past state.

sentence: No podemos salir hasta que no envuelvas los regalos.
why: “hasta que” (until) about an event still to come takes the subjunctive, and the English “until you wrap” shows the subject is tú.

sentence: Correlación no equivale a causalidad.
why: its subject is “Correlación” (correlation), and it states a general truth, so it is the present indicative.

sentence: Puede que me equivoque.
why: the possibility in “Puede que” calls for the subjunctive, and “me” in “me equivoque” shows its subject is yo.

sentence: ¿Y si se equivoca?
why: after “si” (if) the verb stays in the indicative, and the English “What if he's wrong” shows its subject is “he”, in the present.

sentence: No dejes que Tom se escape.
why: letting something happen, “dejes que”, calls for the subjunctive, and its subject is “Tom”, the one who might escape.

sentence: Por favor, escoja a una persona.
why: “Por favor” (please) with the verb first makes a polite command, and the -a ending of this -er verb shows it is addressed to usted.

sentence: Ella no lo escucha.
why: the subject is “Ella” (she), and “no lo escucha” (doesn't listen to him) is a statement about now.

sentence: Escuchemos lo que Tom tiene que decir.
why: it proposes that the speakers listen to Tom, as the English “Let's hear” shows, so it is the nosotros command.

sentence: No escupas por la ventana.
why: it tells someone directly not to do something, “No escupas” (don't spit), and negative commands use this form.

sentence: No me espantes como si fuera un perro.
why: it tells someone directly not to do something, “No me espantes” (don't shoo me), and negative commands use this form.

sentence: Él era mejor de lo que esperaba.
why: no subject is named for it and the English says “than I expected”, so it is yo; the imperfect describes the expectation in the past.

sentence: Ella le espiaba mientras él se estaba bañando.
why: its subject is “Ella” (she), and with “mientras” (while) the imperfect describes an ongoing past action.

sentence: ¿Quieres que espíe a Tom por ti?
why: after “Quieres que” (do you want … to) the subjunctive is used, and the English “want me to spy” shows the speaker is the subject.

sentence: Soy le espose de Tom y uso el pronombre elle.
why: “le espose” here is a gender-neutral noun (spouse), not a form of the verb esposar (to handcuff).

sentence: La Academia Francesa establece las reglas de la lengua nacional.
why: the subject is “La Academia Francesa” (the French Academy), and the sentence states its present role.

sentence: ¡No me estafes!
why: it tells someone directly not to do something, “¡No me estafes!” (don't rip me off), and negative commands use this form.

sentence: Inflamos el globo con cuidado para que no estallara.
why: “para que” (so that) calls for the subjunctive, past after “inflamos” (we blew up), and its subject is “el globo” (the balloon), third person singular.

sentence: Ella está fuera de sí.
why: the subject is “Ella” (she), and the sentence describes her state at this moment.

sentence: Él tiene al profesor en alta estima.
why: here “estima” is the noun “esteem” in “en alta estima” (in high esteem), not a form of the verb estimar.

sentence: Su deseo de ser médica la estimulaba a seguir.
why: its subject is “Su deseo de ser médica” (her desire to be a doctor), and it describes an ongoing influence in the past, so it is the imperfect.

sentence: Estira la lengua, por favor.
why: it is a request to one person, “Estira la lengua, por favor” (stick out your tongue, please), so it is the tú command.

sentence: El coche de Yanni casi se estrella en una cuneta.
why: its subject is “El coche de Yanni” (Yanni's car), and “casi se estrella” (nearly crashed) uses the present, as Spanish does with “casi” (nearly) for a near miss.

sentence: No quiero que Tom nos lo estropee.
why: after “No quiero que” (don't want … to), a wish, the subjunctive is used, and its subject is “Tom”.

sentence: Él le dijo que estudiara.
why: a reported request after “Él le dijo que” (he told her to) takes the subjunctive, and its subject is the person told, “le” (her).

sentence: Intenta investigar en profundidad los valores culturales que evidencia tu texto.
why: its subject is “tu texto” (your text), placed after the verb in “que evidencia tu texto” (that the text reveals), and the present describes what it shows.

sentence: La divisa única evidencia la disparidad de poder adquisitivo y renta entre países.
why: its subject is “La divisa única” (the single currency), and the present states what it reveals.

sentence: Ella lo evitaba siempre que era posible.
why: the subject is “Ella” (she), and the imperfect with “siempre que” (whenever) describes a repeated habit in the past.

sentence: Lavarse las manos evita muchas enfermedades.
why: its subject is the infinitive phrase “Lavarse las manos” (washing your hands), which takes the third person singular, and the sentence states a general fact.

sentence: No me importa que me evites.
why: the feeling in “No me importa que” calls for the subjunctive, and the English “you shun me” shows its subject is tú.

sentence: Un idioma es un sistema vivo que evoluciona con el tiempo.
why: its subject is “que”, standing for “un sistema vivo” (a living system), and it states a general fact, so it is the present indicative.

sentence: Te he dicho un millón de veces que no exageres.
why: “que no exageres” reports what the speaker has told the listener (“Te he dicho”, have told you), and a reported request takes the subjunctive, with tú as its subject.

sentence: Deberías ir a que te examinen la cabeza.
why: “ir a que” (go so that) expresses purpose and takes the subjunctive; no subject is named, so it is the impersonal third-person plural for whoever does the examining.

sentence: Me gustaría que un hombre me examinara.
why: after “Me gustaría que” (would like), a wish in the conditional, the imperfect subjunctive is used, and its subject is “un hombre” (a man).

sentence: Este museo exhibe una fascinante colección de objetos celtas.
why: its subject is “Este museo” (this museum), and it describes a present fact, so it is the present indicative.

sentence: El jefe de Tom exige mucho trabajo.
why: its subject is “El jefe de Tom” (Tom's boss), and the present describes what he habitually demands.

sentence: El futuro no existe: es lo que hacemos.
why: the subject is “El futuro” (the future), and the sentence states a general truth in the present.

sentence: Muchos astrónomos asumen que el universo se expande infinitamente.
why: its subject is “el universo” (the universe), and after the affirmative “asumen que” (assume that) it is stated as fact, so it is the present indicative.

sentence: ¿Querés que te lo explique?
why: the wish in “Querés que” calls for the subjunctive, and the English “want me to explain” shows its subject is yo.

sentence: ¿Preferirías que te explorara una enfermera?
why: its subject is “una enfermera” (a nurse); the preference “Preferirías que” (would … prefer that) takes the subjunctive, imperfect because the preference is hypothetical.

sentence: La compañía explotaba a sus trabajadores con bajos salarios.
why: its subject is “La compañía” (the company), and the imperfect describes its ongoing practice in the past.

sentence: No lo expongas a la lluvia.
why: “No lo expongas” is a direct command telling tú not to expose it, and negative commands use this form.

sentence: El ADN se extrae de una muestra de sangre.
why: its subject is “El ADN” (DNA), with passive “se” (is extracted), and the present describes a general procedure.

sentence: ¿Debería hacer que me extraigan el diente?
why: after “hacer que” (have … do), the subjunctive is used; no subject is named, so it is the impersonal third-person plural for whoever extracts the tooth.

sentence: Sé que Tom te extraña.
why: its subject is “Tom” in “que Tom te extraña” (that Tom misses you), a statement about now.

sentence: Esta compañía fabrica doscientos autos por día.
why: its subject is “Esta compañía” (this company), and “por día” (per day) marks a present routine.

sentence: Esta aplicación nos facilita mucho el trabajo.
why: its subject is “Esta aplicación” (this app), and the present describes its current effect.

sentence: ¿Es cierto que el jengibre facilita la circulación y mejora el metabolismo?
why: its subject is “el jengibre” (ginger), and the present states the general claim asked about with “Es cierto que” (is it true that).

sentence: Tom espera heredar mucho dinero cuando su madre fallezca.
why: “cuando” (when) about a future event takes the subjunctive, and its subject is “su madre” (his mother).

sentence: El problema es que nos falta dinero.
why: like “gustar”, its subject is the thing missing, “dinero” (money), with “nos” as those who lack it, so it is third person singular, in the present.

sentence: ¿Había alguien más que faltara?
why: the relative clause after “alguien más que” (anybody else who) refers to an unknown person in a question, which calls for the subjunctive; its subject “que” stands for “alguien”.

sentence: A mi hija le fascina la música de los años ochenta.
why: its subject is “la música” (music), what pleases in “le fascina” (she loves), so it is the present indicative, third person singular.

sentence: Parecía que a él le fascinaba mucho la música.
why: its subject is “la música” (music), which fascinated “a él” (him), and after “Parecía que” (it seemed that) it describes an ongoing state, so it is the imperfect.

sentence: El vestido, carente de forma, no favorecía nada su figura atlética.
why: its subject is “El vestido” (the dress), and the imperfect describes a past state.

sentence: Ella echó una ojeada al registro para ver si su nombre figuraba en él.
why: its subject is “su nombre” (her name), and the imperfect matches the past “echó” (skimmed), describing a state at that time.

sentence: Esto no figuraba en mis planes.
why: its subject is “Esto” (this), and the imperfect describes a past state of the plans.

sentence: Mi nombre no figura en la lista.
why: its subject is “Mi nombre” (my name), and the present states a current fact.

sentence: ¿Cómo puedo hacer que Tom se fije en mí?
why: making someone do something, “hacer que”, calls for the subjunctive, and its subject is “Tom”.

sentence: Estaré en problemas si la historia se filtra.
why: its subject is “la historia” (the story), and a condition with “si” (if) about the future takes the present indicative in Spanish.

sentence: La vida es un castigo que jamás finaliza.
why: its subject is “que” (that), standing for “un castigo” (a punishment), and “jamás” (never) with the present states a general truth.

sentence: No finjas que no sabes.
why: “No finjas” is a direct command telling tú not to pretend, and negative commands use this form.

sentence: ¡No finja usted lo que no siente!
why: “¡No finja usted…!” is a direct command telling “usted” not to pretend, and negative commands use this form.

sentence: Creo que estoy en lo firme.
why: here “firme” is part of the expression “en lo firme” (in the right), an adjective used as a noun, not a form of the verb “firmar”.

sentence: A esa hora el tráfico fluía sin problemas.
why: its subject is “el tráfico” (the traffic), and it describes an ongoing situation “a esa hora” (at that hour) in the past, so it is the imperfect.

sentence: El Rin fluye entre Francia y Alemania.
why: its subject is “El Rin” (the Rhine), and the present states a geographical fact.

sentence: No seré yo quien fomente un conflicto armado por un quítame allá esas pajas.
why: its subject is “quien” (the one who), which takes the third person even when it means the speaker, and the hypothetical act after “No seré” (won't be) takes the subjunctive.

sentence: Esa universidad forma muy buenos ingenieros.
why: its subject is “Esa universidad” (that university), and the sentence states a general fact about it, so it is the present indicative.

sentence: Dicen que el zen fortalece nuestra mente.
why: its subject is “el zen”, and “Dicen que” (people say that) reports a general claim as fact, so it is the present indicative.

sentence: Odio que me fotografíen.
why: after “Odio que” (hate it when), a feeling, the subjunctive is used, and with no subject named the third person plural means people in general.

sentence: Si él fracasa, ¿y qué?
why: “Si” (if) introducing a real condition takes the present, and its subject is “él” (he).

sentence: Nos fugamos para casarnos sin pensárnoslo. ¡Fue tan romántico!
why: the next sentence, “¡Fue tan romántico!” (it was so romantic), and the English “We eloped” show a completed event in the past, so it is the preterite.

sentence: No fumes estando de servicio.
why: it directly tells tú not to smoke on duty, with “No fumes” (don't smoke), and negative commands use this form.

sentence: La otra no funciona.
why: the subject is “La otra” (the other one), and “no funciona” (doesn't work) describes it now.

sentence: No se ve que funcione.
why: the doubt in “No se ve que” (it doesn't look as if) calls for the subjunctive, and its subject is the thing, “It” in the English.

sentence: Mi hermana gana bien en su trabajo.
why: the subject is “Mi hermana” (my sister), and “gana bien en su trabajo” (earns well at her job) describes her now.

sentence: Ella gana más de lo que gasta.
why: its subject is “Ella” (she), carried over from “Ella gana” (she earns), and the present states a general fact.

sentence: El perro gemía en la puerta porque quería salir.
why: its subject is “el perro” (the dog), and it describes ongoing background in the past alongside “quería” (wanted), so it is the imperfect.

sentence: La persona herida gemía de dolor después de recuperarse de la anestesia.
why: its subject is “La persona herida” (the injured person), and it describes an ongoing action in the past, so it is the imperfect.

sentence: El dinero gobierna el mundo.
why: its subject is “El dinero” (money), and the present states a general truth.

sentence: Gozamos mucho en la fiesta.
why: “en la fiesta” (at the party) refers to a finished event, and the English “We had a very good time” shows the preterite with subject we.

sentence: Hoy es un día lleno de goce.
why: here “goce” is the noun “joy” in “lleno de goce” (full of joy), not a form of the verb gozar.

sentence: No le grites a él.
why: it directly tells tú not to yell at him, with “No le grites” (don't yell), and negative commands use this form.

sentence: ¡No me grités en el oído!
why: it directly tells vos not to scream, with “No me grités” (don't scream at me), and negative commands use this form.

sentence: Gruñía porque no le pagaban bastante.
why: no subject is named, and the English “He grumbled” makes it third person; with “pagaban” (were paying) it describes an ongoing situation in the past, so it is the imperfect.

sentence: Él siempre gruñe como un oso.
why: its subject is “Él” (he), and “siempre” (always) marks a habit, so it is the present indicative.

sentence: Guarda la ropa en el clóset, por favor.
why: the sentence opens with the verb, names no subject and asks the listener, with “por favor” (please), to put the clothes away, so it is a command to tú.

sentence: A ella le gusta ella.
why: with “gustar” the thing liked is the subject, here the second “ella” (her), so it is third person singular, in the present.

sentence: ¿Gusta un tinto, doctor?
why: it is a polite question to “doctor”, addressed as usted, which takes this third-person form; it offers a coffee now.

sentence: Los lugareños creen que en este árbol habita un espíritu.
why: its subject is “un espíritu” (a spirit), and after the affirmative “creen que” (believe that) the belief is stated as fact, so it is the present indicative.

sentence: No era de eso de lo que ella hablaba.
why: its subject is “ella” (she) in “de lo que ella hablaba”, and the imperfect describes what she was talking about at the time.

sentence: El que busca halla.
why: its subject is “El que busca” (the one who searches), and the saying states a timeless truth in the present.

sentence: Debes elegir entre honra y muerte.
why: here “honra” is the noun “honor” in “entre honra y muerte” (between honor and death), not a form of the verb honrar.

sentence: ¡Humilla la vista cuando hables conmigo!
why: it is an exclamatory command, “¡Humilla la vista…!” (lower your eyes), to the person addressed with “hables” (you speak), so it is the tú command.

sentence: Ignora lo que dijo Tom.
why: the sentence opens with the verb and tells the listener to disregard what Tom said (“Ignore”), so it is a command to tú.

sentence: Si fuera tú, lo ignoraría.
why: the condition “Si fuera tú” (if … were you) and the English “I would ignore it” show the speaker is the subject of the conditional.

sentence: El sol lo ilumina todo con su luz.
why: its subject is “El sol” (the sun), and the present states a general truth.

sentence: Sólo imita lo que haga él.
why: it is an instruction, “Sólo imita lo que haga” (just imitate whatever … does), as the English “Just imitate” confirms, so it is the tú command.

sentence: No pude entender qué me impedía moverme.
why: its subject is “qué” (what), a third-person singular pronoun, and the imperfect describes an ongoing situation in the past, at the time of “No pude entender”.

sentence: El dominio de una lengua extranjera implica mucha paciencia.
why: its subject is “El dominio” (the mastery), a singular noun, and the sentence states a general truth in the present.

sentence: No me implique usted en ese asunto.
why: “No me implique usted” is a direct command telling “usted” not to involve the speaker, and negative commands use this form.

sentence: Su silencio implica que está de acuerdo.
why: its subject is “Su silencio” (his silence), and the present states what it means now.

sentence: Colombia importa maquinaria de Europa.
why: the subject is “Colombia”, and the sentence states a general fact about its trade now.

sentence: No me importaba lo que tenía que hacer.
why: like “gustar”, its subject is the thing cared about, “lo que tenía que hacer” (what had to be done), with “me” as the person, so it is third person singular.

sentence: Sé que no importa.
why: no subject is named, and the English “that doesn't matter” shows it is a thing, third person singular, in the present.

sentence: La falta de comida y dinero impulsa a las personas a cometer crímenes.
why: its subject is “La falta” (the lack), a singular noun, and the present states a general truth.

sentence: El zambombazo del cohete inaugura las fiestas.
why: its subject is “El zambombazo del cohete” (the rocket blast), and it states what customarily happens, so it is the present indicative.

sentence: Ese hombre se inclina hacia mí como si me conociera.

sentence: No te inclines ante nadie.

sentence: La entrada incluye una bebida.

sentence: El marco de este cuadro puede hacer que la pintura incremente su valor.

sentence: El sonido se incrementa y disminuye.

sentence: Nada indica que se hará algo al respecto.

sentence: Infecta la zona con cólera.

sentence: ¿Cómo influye el Internet a la memoria humana?

sentence: Puede que Mary nos informe.

sentence: Es posible que Tom ingrese a Harvard.

sentence: El poeta es mucho más el que está inspirado que el que inspira.

sentence: Instale el aparato siguiendo las instrucciones del fabricante.

sentence: ¿Vas a dejar que él insulte de esa manera a tu madre?

sentence: Dejaremos que Tom lo intente.

sentence: A Tom no le interesa lo que digan de María.

sentence: Me interesa mucho la cocina japonesa.

sentence: No es algo que me interese.
why: the relative clause after the negated “No es algo que” (it's not something that) calls for the subjunctive, and its subject “que” stands for “algo” (something).

sentence: Bob le dijo a Jane que no interfiera en sus asuntos personales.

sentence: No dejes que nada se interponga entre tú y el éxito.
why: its subject is “nada” (nothing), and “dejes que” (let) takes the subjunctive.

sentence: Los detenidos esperaban a que se les interrogara.
why: after the past “esperaban a que” (were waiting for), the imperfect subjunctive is used, and with impersonal “se les” the verb is third-person singular.

sentence: No me interrumpas cuando estoy hablando.

sentence: Puede que haya otros factores que intervengan en la relación entre estas dos constantes.
why: after “Puede que haya” (there may be), the relative clause about uncertain “otros factores” (other factors) takes the subjunctive, with those factors as its plural subject.

sentence: Mi tío invierte su plata en finca raíz.
why: its subject is “mi tío” (my uncle), and it states what he regularly does, so it is the present indicative.

sentence: Puede que Mary no nos invite.
why: the possibility in “Puede que” calls for the subjunctive, and its subject is “Mary”.

sentence: No quiero que te involucres.
why: “no” negates “quiero que” (don't want … to), a wish about someone else, so the verb is subjunctive, and “te” shows its subject is tú.

sentence: No juegues en el trabajo.
why: it directly tells tú not to play at work, with “No juegues” (don't play), and negative commands use this form.

sentence: Sea lo que sea que él juegue, siempre gana.
why: the open “Sea lo que sea que” (whatever) calls for the subjunctive, and its subject is “él” (he).

sentence: No me creerán aunque les jure que es cierto.
why: “aunque” (even if) introduces a hypothetical and takes the subjunctive; the English “even if I swear” shows the speaker is the subject.

sentence: ¿Qué justifica eso?
why: its subject is “Qué” (what), and the present asks about the situation now.

sentence: La Luna no escucha cuando el perro ladra.
why: its subject is “el perro” (the dog), and “cuando” (when) describes a general, repeated situation, so it is the present indicative.

sentence: Ella se lamía los dedos.
why: its subject is “Ella” (she), and it describes an ongoing action in the past, so it is the imperfect.

sentence: No quiero que Tom se lastime.
why: “no quiero que” (don't want … to) expresses a wish, so the verb after “que” is subjunctive, and its subject “Tom” is third person singular.

sentence: Sé que nunca dejarías que Tom me lastimara.
why: after “nunca dejarías que” (would never let), a conditional, the clause after “que” takes the imperfect subjunctive, with “Tom” as its subject.

sentence: Mi corazón late rápido cada vez que la veo.
why: its subject is “Mi corazón” (my heart), and “cada vez que” (each time) marks a present habit.

sentence: Ella se lava la cabeza.
why: the subject is “Ella” (she), and the English “She's washing” shows it is happening now.

sentence: Lee lo que quieras.
why: the English “Read whatever you like” is a command, and “quieras” shows it is addressed to tú.

sentence: Levanta la mano si sabes la respuesta.

sentence: Al fin nos libramos de él.

sentence: La innovación marca la diferencia entre quien lidera y quien obedece.

sentence: Mi mujer Lidia es una mujer inteligente y bonita.
why: here “Lidia” is a woman's name (“Mi mujer Lidia”), not a form of the verb lidiar.

sentence: La gravedad liga los planetas al Sol.
why: its subject is “La gravedad” (gravity), and it states a general truth, so it is the present indicative.

sentence: México es un país que limita con los Estados Unidos.
why: its subject is “que” (that), standing for “un país” (a country), and the present states a lasting geographical fact.

sentence: Puede que Mary no lo limpie.
why: the possibility in “Puede que” calls for the subjunctive, and its subject is “Mary”.

sentence: Llamamos a Nueva York la Gran Manzana.

sentence: Esto me llena de alegría.

sentence: Mi hermana llevaba un vestido rojo en la fiesta.

sentence: Espero que no llueva todo el día.

sentence: Lograba todo lo que quería.

sentence: No importa lo que lleve Tom, siempre luce bien.

sentence: ¿Están Mario y Lucía con su padre?

sentence: Cuando esté enfadado, cuente hasta cuatro. Cuando esté muy enfadado, maldiga.

sentence: Mi hermano maltrataba sus juguetes y siempre los rompía.

sentence: No te maltrates a ti mismo sobre ello.

sentence: El bebé se queda dormido mientras mama.

sentence: A Tom no le gusta la gente que manipula a otras personas.

sentence: Le dije a Tom que se mantuviera lejos de María.

sentence: Mire lo que marca la caja.

sentence: Esa medicina mata las bacterias.

sentence: ¿Cuánto mide de alto la Torre Eiffel?

sentence: No quiero que ella se meta en problemas.

sentence: Lo mezclamos con lo bueno, no lo malo.

sentence: Me duele la muela del juicio superior derecha.

sentence: No me molesta lo que estás haciendo.

sentence: No quiero que se molesten.

sentence: Nos dijeron que no molestemos a Tom.

sentence: Ella no lo pudo convencer de que montara un caballo.

sentence: El perro mueve la cola cuando me ve.

sentence: Le dije a Tom que no se moviera.

sentence: Te dije que no te muevas.

sentence: El río Magdalena nace en el sur del país.

sentence: La ley obliga a las empresas a pagar impuestos.

sentence: La mujer observa y el hombre piensa.
why: the subject is “La mujer” (the woman), and the sentence states a general claim in the present.

sentence: ¿Por qué no se me ocurriría a mí?

sentence: Él odia a los padres de ella.

sentence: El dinero no huele.

sentence: Mi profesor me orienta con la tesis.

sentence: Debemos descubrir dónde se origina este fuego.

sentence: El médico dice que el bebé orina muy poco.
why: its subject is “el bebé” (the baby), and the present describes what usually happens.

sentence: Queremos estar en Tokio antes de que oscurezca.

sentence: Oye lo que tengo que decir.

sentence: Antes padecía de fuertes migrañas ocasionales pero, afortunadamente, ahora son mucho menos intensas.

sentence: María padece una seria enfermedad.

sentence: Eso es por lo que se le paga a Tom.

sentence: Le dijeron que se parara, y eso hizo.
why: a reported request after “Le dijeron que” (he was told to) takes the subjunctive, and its subject is the person told, “Le” (him).

sentence: Esto no es lo que parece.
why: its subject is “lo que” (what), referring back to “Esto” (this), and the present “es” (is) sets the time.

sentence: Parecía que él estaba bien.

sentence: ¿Qué te parece si vamos a cine el sábado?

sentence: Le dije a Tom que pare.
why: “que pare” (to stop) is a form of parar (to stop), not of parir (to give birth).

sentence: ¿Partimos la torta ahora o después?

sentence: El bus pasa por mi casa cada diez minutos.
why: the subject is “El bus” (the bus), and “cada diez minutos” (every ten minutes) marks a regular, present habit.

sentence: Pasamos la Navidad en Hawái.
why: the English “We spent” shows a completed event in the past, one Christmas spent in Hawaii, so it is the preterite.

sentence: Pase, por favor, y siéntese aquí.

sentence: Sé lo que pasa.
why: its subject is “lo que” (what), and the English “what's going on” shows something happening now.

sentence: Él pasea a su perro cada mañana.

sentence: Espero que este caballo no patee.

sentence: Este caballo patea cuando alguien se le acerca por detrás.

sentence: Mientras patinaba sobre el pavimento húmedo, mi cabeza rebotó en el bordillo.

sentence: No olvides tus patines de hielo.

sentence: Un guardia patrulla el conjunto residencial por las noches.

sentence: Tú no tienes ninguna peca.

sentence: Ese color no pega con tu camisa.

sentence: Esta noche hace un frío que pela.

sentence: La luz penetra la oscuridad.
why: its subject is “La luz” (the light), and the sentence states a general fact, so it is the present indicative.

sentence: Pensaba que eras de Boston.
why: no subject is named and the English says “I thought”; the imperfect describes what was in the speaker's mind.

sentence: Pensamos ir a Cartagena en diciembre.

sentence: Su perfume se percibe a cien metros de distancia.

sentence: No la pierdas de vista.

sentence: No se pierde lo que no se tiene.

sentence: Ella quiere que yo te perdone.
why: the wish in “quiere que” calls for the subjunctive, and its subject is “yo” (I).

sentence: Fumar te perjudica.
why: its subject is “Fumar” (smoking), and it states a general fact, so it is the present indicative.

sentence: Ella fue a verlo mientras permanecía en Boston.
why: no subject is named and the English “while he was staying” shows it is “he”; the imperfect describes his ongoing stay.

sentence: Los hombres vienen y van, pero la tierra permanece.
why: the subject is “la tierra” (the earth), and the saying states a timeless truth in the present.

sentence: Me dijeron que permaneciera en el coche.
why: a reported request after “Me dijeron que” takes the subjunctive, and the person told, “Me”, is its subject, so it is yo.

sentence: A Tom se le permite hacerlo, pero no a Mary.
why: impersonal “se le permite” (one allows him) has no personal subject and takes the third person singular, here in the present.

sentence: Él no pertenece a la ciudad.
why: the subject is “Él” (he), and “no pertenece a la ciudad” (doesn't belong in the city) describes him now.

sentence: Nada le perturba.
why: its subject is “Nada” (nothing), and it states a lasting fact, so it is the present indicative.

sentence: Ella te mostrará cómo se pesca.

sentence: El pollito pía.

sentence: El polluelo piaba pidiendo comida.
why: its subject is “El polluelo” (the chick), and with “pidiendo comida” (begging for food) it describes an ongoing action in the past, so it is the imperfect.

sentence: Casi me pilla un coche.
why: its subject is “un coche” (a car); Spanish uses the present after “Casi” (almost) to recount a near miss.

sentence: Lo pillamos tratando de salir de su cuarto.
why: the English “We caught him” shows a completed past event, so it is the preterite with subject we.

sentence: Mi hija pinta un perro en su cuaderno.
why: the subject is “Mi hija” (my daughter), and the English “is drawing” shows it is happening now.

sentence: Si Tom planeaba casarse, me lo hubiera dicho

sentence: Plante un árbol por allí.

sentence: Puede que Tom esté fuera.

sentence: Ella porta una pulsera de plata en la muñeca.

sentence: Siempre que mira a sus sobrinos, se posa en su mirada un brillo nostálgico.

sentence: Él vendió todo lo que poseía.

sentence: El rayo precede al trueno.

why: “hasta que” (until) about a future change takes the subjunctive, and the verb is impersonal, about the weather (“until it is warmer”), so it is third person singular.

sentence: Él tiende a tomarse las cosas demasiado en serio.
why: its subject is “Él” (he), and the present describes his general tendency.

sentence: El demonio tienta la carne.
why: its subject is “El demonio” (the demon), and it states a general truth, so it is the present indicative.

sentence: Deja que termine, ¿no?
why: the request “Deja que” (let) calls for the subjunctive, and the English “Let me finish” shows its subject is yo.

sentence: Siempre terminamos peleando por lo mismo.
why: the English “We always end up” and “Siempre” (always) describe a regular habit in the present.

sentence: El bebé deja de llorar apenas le dan teta.
why: “teta” here is the noun (teat) in “dan teta” (they breastfeed him), not a form of the verb tetar.

sentence: La gata les da teta a sus cuatro gatitos.
why: “teta” here is the noun (teat) in “les da teta” (nurses them), not a form of the verb tetar.

sentence: Le di la teta a mi bebé.
why: here “teta” is the noun “breast” in “Le di la teta” (breastfed), not a form of the verb tetar.

sentence: No tires esa camisa, todavía sirve.
why: it directly tells tú not to throw the shirt away, with “No tires” (don't throw away), and negative commands use this form.

sentence: Alguien toca la puerta.
why: the subject is “Alguien” (someone), and the English “is knocking” shows it is happening now.

sentence: Hoy te toca lavar los platos.
why: in “te toca” (it's your turn) the task “lavar los platos” is the subject, so it is third person singular, and “Hoy” (today) puts it in the present.

sentence: Nos topamos el uno al otro en la estación.
why: the English “We ran into each other” describes a single completed meeting in the past, so it is the preterite.

sentence: El camino tuerce a la derecha después del puente.
why: its subject is “el camino” (the road), and it describes where the road goes, so it is the present indicative.

sentence: El problema torturaba al jefe.
why: its subject is “El problema” (the problem), and the imperfect describes an ongoing state in the past.

sentence: Torturamos a mi papá con la misma canción todo el viaje.
why: the English “we tortured” and “todo el viaje” (the whole trip) present a finished trip seen as a whole, so it is the preterite.

sentence: Él trabaja de la mañana a la noche.
why: the subject is “Él” (he), and “de la mañana a la noche” (from morning till evening) describes his usual day now.

sentence: Él traduce más rápido de lo que otros leen.
why: its subject is “Él” (he), and the present describes his general ability.

sentence: La historia transcurre en Lisboa.
why: its subject is “La historia” (the story), and it says where the story is set, a timeless fact, so it is the present indicative.

sentence: La Voz de América transmite desde Washington.
why: its subject is “La Voz de América” (Voice of America), and the present describes its regular broadcasting.

sentence: La lectura me transporta a un otro mundo.
why: its subject is “La lectura” (reading), and the present states a general effect.

sentence: Tomás quiere que me traslade a Boston.
why: after “quiere que” (wants … to), a wish, the subjunctive is used, and the reflexive “me” and the English “wants me to move” show the speaker is the subject.

sentence: De eso no se trata la pregunta.
why: its subject is “la pregunta” (the question), and “no se trata” (is not about) is a statement about now.

sentence: No trates de hacer todo a la vez.
why: it directly tells tú not to try, with “No trates de” (don't try to), and negative commands use this form.

sentence: Sabía que se trataba de Tom.
why: impersonal “se trataba de” (it was about) has no personal subject and always takes the third person singular; it describes the past situation.

sentence: Nuestra oficina se ubica en el centro de la ciudad.
why: its subject is “Nuestra oficina” (our office), and the present describes where it is located.

sentence: Este puente une los dos lados del río.
why: its subject is “Este puente” (this bridge), and the sentence states what the bridge does, so it is the present indicative.

sentence: No quiero que me usen.
why: the wish in “No quiero que” calls for the subjunctive; no subject is named, so it is the impersonal “they” (people), as the English passive “to be used” shows.

sentence: No quiero que me utilicen.
why: the wish in “No quiero que” calls for the subjunctive; no subject is named, so it is the impersonal “they” (people), as the English passive “to be used” shows.

sentence: Mary vaga de un sitio a otro.
why: its subject is “Mary”, and it describes what she habitually does, so it is the present indicative.

sentence: Este documento ya no vale.
why: the subject is “Este documento” (this document), and “ya no vale” (is no longer valid) describes it now.

sentence: No se valora la salud hasta que viene la enfermedad.
why: its subject is “la salud” (health), with passive “se” (is valued), and the present states a general truth.

sentence: El precio varía con la demanda.
why: its subject is “El precio” (the price), and the present states a general rule.

sentence: Este banco siempre vela por sus propios intereses.
why: its subject is “Este banco” (this bank), and “siempre” (always) marks a habit, so it is the present indicative.

sentence: Verifica la veracidad de este artículo.
why: the sentence opens with the verb and tells the reader to check the article (“Verifica la veracidad”, check the accuracy), so it is a command to tú.

sentence: Ella se vestía como un niño.
why: its subject is “Ella” (she), and the imperfect describes how she habitually dressed in the past.

sentence: Es la casa en la que vive él.
why: its subject is “él” (he) in “en la que vive él” (that he lives in), and “Es” (is) shows the present.

sentence: Vivimos días muy felices en esa casa.
why: the English “We lived through” and “esa casa” (that house) show a completed period in the past, so it is the preterite.

sentence: Vivimos en la Tierra.
why: the English “We live” states a lasting fact about where we live, “en la Tierra” (on Earth), so it is the present.

sentence: Volamos de Londres a Nueva York.
why: the English “We flew” shows a completed trip in the past, so it is the preterite.

sentence: Le dije que no volviera.
why: a reported request after “Le dije que” (told him that) takes the subjunctive, and its subject is the person told, “le” (him).

sentence: El gato yacía dormido al sol.
why: its subject is “el gato” (the cat), and it describes a past state, “dormido al sol” (asleep in the sun), so it is the imperfect.
